statements.t: As of November 11, 2026, we expect to sign the Merger Agreement in the very near term.
The proposed transaction is intended to combine our digital mortgage, lending, and title platform with TYTL’s blockchain-based real estate digital asset platform.

With MagicBlocks’ capabilities fully integrated, we expect to accelerate product innovation while supporting future initiatives across mortgage origination, title services, home equity products, and digital real estate transactions, reduce production costs, and improve the speed and consistency of the borrower experience.
Our operating results are expected to remain sensitive to interest rate fluctuations and broader macroeconomic conditions.
We expect housing supply, affordability, and demographic trends to remain important drivers of purchase mortgage demand and our future operating performance.

Our technology initiatives are intended to improve workflow automation, data integration, underwriting support, document processing, and communication among borrowers, lending professionals, and third-party service providers.

We also intend to evaluate opportunities to expand our home financing product offerings to address a broader range of consumer needs, including purchase mortgages, refinancing, and home equity financing solutions.
These initiatives are intended to diversify revenue opportunities, improve customer engagement, and strengthen our competitive position.

We expect customer acquisition efficiency, borrower conversion rates, and operating leverage to remain important factors affecting our future revenues, profitability, and overall financial performance.
The Company therefore cannot predict whether future policy actions will reduce mortgage rates or improve mortgage origination volumes.

During the third quarter, the Company continued to focus on higher-margin non-QM products, including bank statement and debt service coverage ratio loans, and on technology intended to improve loan pricing, customer acquisition and operating efficiency.

On October 20, 2026, the Company announced an additional operating-expense reduction plan targeting approximately $0.3 million of monthly savings, or $3.0 million on an annualized basis, incremental to cost reductions implemented earlier in 2026.
The Company estimated that it would incur approximately $0.3 million of one-time transition costs through December 1, 2026, after which it expects the full monthly savings to be realized.
The Company expects that the actions, together with its investment in automation and higher-value products, will reduce its fixed-cost structure and improve operating leverage.

Of the anticipated nine million merger shares that the Company’s CEO will receive, he will cancel one third of those shares, assuming closing, to support Company’s capital-raising initiatives, potentially reducing dilution to existing shareholders.

This non-GAAP financial measure should not be considered in isolation and is not intended to be a substitute for any GAAP financial measures, but rather provides supplemental information that we believe helps investors better understand our business, our business model, and how we analyze our performance.

Accordingly, other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate similarly titled non-GAAP financial measures differently or may use other measures to evaluate their performance, all of which could reduce the usefulness of our non-GAAP financial measures as tools for comparison.
We intend to maintain a disciplined financial policy and improve our credit metrics, which are critical to our lending partners.

The availability of additional financing will be largely dependent on our common stock price and liquidity as we utilize our ELOC and ATM Agreements as well as on our operating success, including improved margins as well as operational improvements, which will be necessary to attract investors.
However, there can be no assurance that we will be successful in securing the necessary capital on favorable terms, or at all.

If there is an indication of impairment, management would prepare an estimate of future cash flows (undiscounted and without interest charges) expected to result from the use of the asset and its eventual disposition.

estimates.name: Revenue recognition — Gains on Sale of Loans, Net
estimates.t: See discussion above under “Mortgage Loans Held for Sale and Gain on Sale of Loans Revenue Recognition” and below under “Derivative Financial Instruments and Revenue Recognition.”

estimates.name: Loan Origination Fees and Costs
estimates.t: Loan origination fees represent revenue earned from originating mortgage loans.

estimates.name: Interest Income
estimates.t: Interest income on mortgage loans held for sale is recognized for the period from loan funding to sale based upon the principal balance outstanding and contractual interest rates.

estimates.name: Interest Expense
estimates.t: Interest expense relating to the warehouse lines of credit is included in net revenues.

estimates.name: Title Fees
estimates.t: Settlement fees and commissions are earned at loan settlement.

estimates.name: Fractional Equity Revenues, Related Party
estimates.t: The Company receives a transaction fee of 3.5% of the amount of equity sold by homeowners to TYTL for customer service, transaction processing and platform support.

estimates.name: Other Revenues
estimates.t: Goodwill is the excess of the purchase price over the estimated fair value of identifiable net assets acquired in business combinations.

statements.t: Of the anticipated nine million TYTL merger shares to be issued to Beeline’s CEO Nick Liuzza upon closing, approximately three million shares will be forfeited and cancelled, reducing potential dilution for existing Beeline shareholders and supporting the Company’s future capital-raising efforts.
Management expects fourth-quarter seasonality and impact from a challenging interest-rate environment.
